paragraphs: Here's what I see in Luke 9:10-17, friend: the Twelve look at the crowd and see a problem too big for them. They ask Jesus to dismiss the crowd because "we are in a desolate place here." (Luke 9:12) Then Jesus tells them, "You give them something to eat." (Luke 9:13) I think that's the moment that matters most.

Look at what the Twelve bring Him: "only five loaves of bread and two fish." (Luke 9:13) That's NOT much, and Jesus still tells them to feed the crowd. He takes what they hand over, looks up to heaven, speaks a blessing and breaks it, and then it goes back through their hands to the people. (Luke 9:16) So the lesson is that Jesus works with what you hand Him, and a small offering is plenty in His hands.

And look how it ends: "They all ate and were satisfied," with twelve basketfuls left over. (Luke 9:17) The disciples started with five loaves and two fish, and they ended up carrying more than they started with. So when your day feels like a desolate place and your supply looks tiny, bring it to Jesus anyway. I'm still amazed He called a worn-out stamper out of a junk drawer to bake cookies, so I know He loves to use small things, and you can keep your hands open, baker.
